# Global Semiconductor Equipment — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R6 Hardened)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 wafer fab equipment makers across 8 research dimensions.

---

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker | HQ |
|---|--------|--------|----|
| 1 | ASML | ASML | Netherlands |
| 2 | Applied Materials | AMAT | USA |
| 3 | Lam Research | LRCX | USA |
| 4 | Tokyo Electron | 8035.T | Japan |
| 5 | KLA | KLAC | USA |
| 6 | Advantest | 6857.T | Japan |
| 7 | SCREEN Semiconductor | 7735.T | Japan |
| 8 | Teradyne | TER | USA |

---

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. WFE Revenue per Tool Installed: Revenue / 2024 Tool Shipment Units**
For each entity: FY2024 revenue, FY2024 total tool shipment units (from annual report + sellside sampling). Compute $M revenue per tool. Rank. Identify why ASML's ratio is ~10x LRCX's (EUV pricing vs etch tool pricing). Which companies' ratios are declining 2022→2024?

**Q2. End-Market Rev × Implied WFE Intensity**
End-market split (Logic/Memory/Analog) × industry WFE intensity (capex/fab revenue ratio varies by process). Compute implied "weighted WFE intensity" per entity. The entity with highest weighted intensity is most levered to the 2025-27 cycle — identify and justify.

**Q3. China Revenue Run-off Curve 2024-27**
For each entity, model a 3-year China revenue decline curve assuming Sep 2024 BIS rules fully enforced + continuing escalation. Provide: 2024 China revenue, 2025E, 2026E, 2027E. Key assumption: mature node (≥28nm) WFE still shippable to China; advanced node (≤14nm logic, ≤18nm DRAM) restricted. What % of each entity's China revenue is mature node vs restricted advanced? Cite disclosure source.

**Q4. Service Revenue Margin Accretion**
Service revenue is typically 50-70% gross margin vs 35-45% for equipment. For each entity: (a) service revenue FY24, (b) estimate service operating margin from mix math, (c) show how service growth FY24-FY27 would affect blended company OM. Rank by "service lever" potential.

**Q5. R&D per Incremental Revenue $**
Compute: 2022-2024 cumulative R&D / (2024 revenue − 2022 revenue). This "R&D productivity" ratio penalizes companies spending on R&D without revenue growth payoff. Identify the most and least productive R&D spenders. (Note: this is unusual but illustrative for cyclical industries).

**Q6. Book-to-Bill Cycle Position Inference**
Using Q1 2023 through Q4 2024 quarterly book-to-bill data, identify each entity's current cycle position: early recovery / mid recovery / late recovery / peak / late peak. Compare to 2019-2020 cycle for analogous positioning. Specifically: is Advantest at "peak HBM cycle" (i.e., risk of disappointment ahead)?

**Q7. HBM Revenue per HBM-Capable Fab**
For the HBM-exposed names (Advantest, AMAT, LRCX, TEL): HBM-related revenue / number of HBM-capable fabs globally (primarily SK hynix + Micron + Samsung, ~15 fabs 2024). Rank by revenue intensity per HBM fab. Which entity captures the most value per HBM facility and why?

**Q8. Scenario: Dual Shock — China -50% + Memory -30%**
Harder scenario: **simultaneous** China WFE -50% AND memory capex -30% in 2026 (recession scenario). For each entity, compute compound revenue impact using 2024 revenue decomposition. Identify the 2 most resilient and 2 most vulnerable names. Management-announced mitigation (cost cuts, geographic shift): cite specific commentary per company.

**Common Basis**

FX used for cross-company tables: `EUR/USD = 1.08`, `USD/JPY = 151.5`. Japanese companies use the fiscal year ending March 2025 as the closest FY2024 operating year unless noted. Tool-unit, HBM revenue, and China mature/restricted splits are not fully disclosed for most companies, so those items are modeled from public revenue, segment mix, installed-base disclosures, and sell-side ASP sampling.

## Q1. WFE Revenue per 2024 Tool Shipped

| Rank | Company | FY24 revenue | Est. 2024 tool units | Revenue / tool | Disclosure quality |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | ASML | $30.5B | 418 | **$73.0M** | Actual systems: 380 new + 38 used; ASML reports this directly. |
| 2 | KLA | $9.8B | 950 | **$10.3M** | Units modeled; high-ASP inspection/metrology. |
| 3 | Lam Research | $14.9B | 2,100 | **$7.1M** | Units modeled; etch/deposition/clean ASP sampling. |
| 4 | Applied Materials | $27.2B | 5,600 | **$4.9M** | Units modeled; broad lower/mid ASP chamber mix. |
| 5 | Tokyo Electron | $16.1B | 4,400 | **$3.6M** | Units modeled; coater/developer, etch, deposition, clean, prober mix. |
| 6 | SCREEN Semi | $4.1B | 1,650 | **$2.5M** | Units modeled; wet clean tools. |
| 7 | Teradyne | $2.8B | 1,550 | **$1.8M** | Units modeled; ATE systems. |
| 8 | Advantest | $5.1B | 3,200 | **$1.6M** | Units modeled; memory/SoC testers and handlers. |

ASML’s ratio is about **10.3x Lam’s** because one EUV system is a nine-figure tool, and even DUV immersion tools are far above typical etch/deposition/clean chamber pricing. ASML disclosed 2024 revenue of €28.3B, installed-base management sales of €6.494B, and 418 systems sold; Lam disclosed $14.905B FY2024 revenue and $8.922B systems revenue, but not shipped tool count. Sources: [ASML FY2024 results](https://www.asml.com/en/news/press-releases/2025/q4-2024-financial-results), [Lam 2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/707549/000114036124041895/ny20031746x3_ars.pdf).

Ratios likely declined from 2022 to 2024 for **AMAT, LRCX, TEL, KLA, and TER**. ASML rose on EUV/high-NA mix; Advantest rose on HBM tester mix; SCREEN rose on higher semiconductor clean-equipment revenue.

## Q2. End-Market Revenue × Implied WFE Intensity

Assumed industry WFE intensity: leading logic/foundry `~42-45%`, DRAM/HBM `~60%`, NAND `~45%`, analog/mature/specialty `~20-25%`.

| Company | FY24 end-market proxy | Weighted WFE intensity | Cycle leverage |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Advantest | Memory/HBM test ~35%, SoC/compute ~50% | **~50%** | Highest, because HBM drives tester intensity. |
| Lam Research | Memory 42%, foundry 40%, logic/IDM 18% | ~49% | Very high; etch/deposition-heavy DRAM/HBM. |
| Tokyo Electron | DRAM 31%, NAND 7%, non-memory 62% | ~48% | High; HBM DRAM and advanced logic. |
| ASML | Logic ~70%, memory ~30% | ~48% | High; EUV/DUV exposure to leading-edge fabs. |
| Applied Materials | Foundry/logic/other 68%, DRAM 28%, flash 4% | ~47% | High but more diversified. |
| KLA | Logic/foundry-heavy process control, memory ~20% modeled | ~45% | High, less memory torque. |
| Teradyne | Compute/SoC + memory test, robotics dilution | ~43% | Moderate. |
| SCREEN Semi | Clean tools across logic, memory, mature | ~41% | Moderate; China/mature clean exposure. |

Highest weighted cycle leverage: **Advantest**. Its absolute revenue is smaller than AMAT/Lam/TEL, but HBM makes tester demand unusually capital-intensive per dollar of memory output. AMAT’s official FY2024 Semi Systems split was foundry/logic/other 68%, DRAM 28%, flash 4%; TEL disclosed FY2025 SPE new equipment mix of DRAM 31%, NAND 7%, non-memory 62%; Lam disclosed memory 42%, foundry 40%, logic/IDM 18%. Sources: [AMAT FY2024 results](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/), [TEL FY2025 Q4 presentation](https://www.tel.com/ir/library/report/l8gqgo00000000gl-att/fy25q4presentations-e.pdf), [Lam 2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/707549/000114036124041895/ny20031746x3_ars.pdf).

Model: mature-node China revenue remains shippable but fades with localization; restricted advanced-node revenue runs off sharply. BIS’s December 2024 package added controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment, software, HBM, and 140 entities. Source: [BIS press release](https://media.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-strengthens-export-controls-restrict-chinas-capability-produce-advanced-semiconductors-military).

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| AMAT | $10.1B | 80% / 20% | $8.1B | $6.8B | $5.8B |
| TEL | $6.7B | 80% / 20% | $5.4B | $4.5B | $3.8B |

| Teradyne | $0.38B | 75% / 25% | $0.29B | $0.24B | $0.20B |

KLA disclosed China at roughly 42%. Teradyne disclosed China revenue of $375.2M. Sources: [AMAT FY2024 results](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2024/), [Lam 2024 10-K](https://content.edgar-online.com/ExternalLink/EDGAR/0000707549-24-000106.html?dest=lrcx-20240630_htm), [TEL FY2025 Q4 presentation](https://www.tel.com/ir/library/report/l8gqgo00000000gl-att/fy25q4presentations-e.pdf), [KLA 2024 10-K](https://ir.kla.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000319201-24-000021/klac-20240630.htm), [Teradyne 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/97210/000095017025023784/ter-20241231.htm).

## Q6. Book-to-Bill Cycle Position

| Company | Q1 2023-Q4 2024 inference | Current position | 2019-2020 analog |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASML | Book-to-bill fell below 1.0 in most 2024 quarters; Q4 bookings €7.1B vs sales €9.3B. | Early/mid recovery, not peak. | Similar to 2019 digestion before 2020 recovery. |
| AMAT | Orders not fully disclosed; revenue record, China normalizing. | Mid recovery. | 2020-style broad recovery, but with China risk. |
| Lam | Management called WFE recovery early; memory improving from trough. | Early recovery. | Early 2020 memory recovery. |
| TEL | FY2025 recovered strongly; FY2026 guide expects stronger H2. | Mid recovery. | 2020 upturn phase. |
| KLA | Process control recovered, but memory/foundry capex still uneven. | Mid/late recovery. | Later than 2019 trough, not yet 2021 peak. |
| Advantest | HBM/memory tester orders surged. | **Late peak / peak HBM cycle.** | Closer to late-2020/2021 tester upcycle. |
| SCREEN | Strong China/mature-node clean demand. | Late recovery; China peak risk. | 2020 recovery with heavier China mix. |
| Teradyne | Semi test recovering; robotics weak. | Early recovery. | Early-cycle semi-test recovery. |

Advantest is the clearest **peak-HBM-cycle risk**: demand can remain structurally strong, but the order base is already highly HBM-expectation sensitive. Sources include company quarterly/annual releases above, especially ASML bookings disclosure, TEL quarterly application/field-solutions disclosures, and Teradyne’s statement that AI, custom accelerators, networking and HBM drove 2024 test growth: [Teradyne annual report](https://investors.teradyne.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000950170-25-046348/0000950170-25-046348.pdf).

## Q7. HBM Revenue per HBM-Capable Fab

Assumption: ~15 HBM-capable fabs/lines globally across SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron. HBM revenue is not separately disclosed, so this uses HBM-attributable portions of memory test, DRAM WFE, and advanced packaging exposure.

| Rank | Company | Est. 2024 HBM-related revenue | HBM fabs | Revenue / HBM fab | Why |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Advantest | ~$1.1B | 15 | **~$73M** | HBM requires intensive wafer, package, and final test capacity. |
| 2 | Applied Materials | ~$0.9B | 15 | ~$60M | Deposition, CMP, packaging and hybrid-bonding-adjacent process exposure. |
| 3 | Lam Research | ~$0.8B | 15 | ~$53M | DRAM/HBM etch and deposition steps, plus advanced packaging process steps. |
| 4 | Tokyo Electron | ~$0.7B | 15 | ~$47M | DRAM process tools, coater/developer, wafer prober, bonder exposure. |

Advantest captures the most value per HBM facility because HBM stacks increase test time, parallelism needs, thermal/electrical screening, and known-good-die requirements. TEL specifically said DRAM leading-edge investment including HBM significantly contributed to FY2025 sales mix. ## Q5. R&D per Incremental Revenue $ (2022–2024)

### Formula
$$\text{R&D Productivity Ratio} = \frac{\sum \text{R&D}_{2022-2024}}{\text{Revenue}_{2024} - \text{Revenue}_{2022}}$$

A lower ratio = more productive (less R&D per $ of new revenue). A negative or extremely high ratio signals R&D spending without revenue payoff. *(Note: this metric intentionally penalizes cyclical companies in a downturn; it's illustrative, not normative.)*

### Interpretation

- **Least Productive (most penalized)**: Lam Research — spent $4.68B in R&D over 3 years while revenue shrank by $2.32B (NAND WFE collapse). This is a cyclical artifact, not a judgment on Lam's R&D quality.

- **Advantest's high ratio**: R&D spending jumped on HBM/AI test development but FY2024 revenue was still recovering from FY2023 trough (¥331.6B) — FY2022 was the prior peak. Using FY2022→FY2024 masks the V-shaped recovery.

### Why ASML's Ratio is ~10x LRCX's

ASML's EUV systems are among the most complex capital goods ever manufactured — the TWINSCAN NXE:3600D costs ~$180-200M and the new High-NA EUV (EXE:5000) costs ~$380M. ASML's monopoly position (no competitor has produced a working EUV system) means customers pay full replacement value. LRCX sells at scale with more competitive pricing across etch, deposition, and clean.

- **ASML**: Revenue per tool *increased* (ASP mix shift toward EUV and now High-NA EUV). **Not declining.**

### Why ASML's Ratio is ~10x LRCX's

ASML's **$52.5M per tool** vs. Lam's estimated **$4-6M per tool** (etch/deposition tools typically $1-5M each, with Lam shipping hundreds of systems):

1. **EUV pricing dominance**: ASML's EUV systems sell for **€150-350M** per unit (High-NA EUV ~€350M+; DUV ~€50-90M). Each EUV is a complete lithography solution integrating optics, lasers, and stage systems requiring 100,000+ components.
2. **Etch tool pricing**: Lam's etch/deposition systems typically sell for **$1-5M** per unit. Lam ships far more units (est. 1,500-3,000/year) at much lower ASPs.
3. **Monopoly position**: ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography; Lam competes with TEL and AMAT in etch.
4. **Source**: ASML 2024 Annual Report (asml.com/investors/annual-report/2024); Statista system sales by technology data confirming 44 EUV + 374 DUV systems shipped in 2024.

### Ratios Declining 2022→2024

- **ASML**: Revenue grew from €21.2B (2022) to €28.3B (2024) = +33%, but systems shipped likely grew faster (2022: ~32 EUV + 270 DUV ≈ 302 litho; 2024: 44 EUV + 374 DUV = 418 litho, +38%). **Revenue per tool declined** as mix shifted to lower-ASP DUV (ArFi/ArF dry) to meet China mature-node demand.
- **TEL**: Revenue declined from FY2022 ¥2,200B to FY2024 ¥1,830B (-17%), while unit volumes were maintained for mature-node China shipments → ratio declined.
